verdict_reason: The header check works for trader routes, but the admin-route exemptions are untested and duplicated from AdminSecretFilter, the 400 body copies GlobalExceptionHandler without traceId, and a request attribute is written that nothing reads.

todos.issue: REQUEST_ORGANISATION_ID (line 27) is written as a request attribute at line 69 but nothing in src/ reads it: NotificationController takes the organisation again from the header with @RequestHeader(HEADER_ORGANISATION_ID). The attribute is an unreachable second channel for the same value, and its key 'trade.imports.traderOrganisationId' adds a third name for the concept beside the header and the MDC key 'organisationId'.
todos.fix: Must: the organisation id reaches the controller through one channel, and the filter declares nothing no caller uses. One way: delete REQUEST_ORGANISATION_ID and the setAttribute call, leaving the controller's @RequestHeader as the single reader.

todos.issue: Which /notifications routes are admin routes is written twice: here in shouldNotFilter (lines 43-54: DELETE exactly /notifications, POST /notifications/{ref}/replay, plus two GETs) and in AdminSecretFilter.shouldNotFilter (DELETE with uri.startsWith("/notifications"), POST uri.matches("/notifications/[^/]+/replay")). The copies already differ: AdminSecretFilter matches any DELETE under /notifications on getRequestURI, this one only the exact path on servletPath(). A new admin route has to be added in both, and a miss in this one returns 400 to the admin app.
todos.fix: Must: one owner decides whether a request is an admin notification route, and both filters ask it. One way: extract an AdminNotificationRoutes.matches(HttpServletRequest) in the filter package covering all four admin routes; AdminSecretFilter guards its subset and this filter skips all of them.

todos.issue: No test proves the four admin exemptions in shouldNotFilter (lines 43-54). IntegrationBase.webClient always sends Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id as a default header, and the only header-less test (NotificationIT.traderRequests_shouldRejectMissingOrganisationHeader) covers POST /notifications. Deleting any of the four exemption branches leaves every test green, yet the ticket says GET /notifications/reference-numbers, /{ref}/outbox-events, /{ref}/replay and bulk DELETE /notifications stay unscoped for the admin app.
todos.fix: Must: a test fails if any admin route starts demanding the organisation header, and a test fails if a trader route (e.g. GET /notifications, GET /{ref}/fulfilments) stops demanding it. One way: a parameterised NotificationIT case that strips the header and calls each admin route expecting its normal status, plus a parameterised case over the trader routes expecting 400.

todos.issue: logAndReject (lines 81-86) hand-builds the 400 problem body (type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/bad-request, title 'Bad Request') that GlobalExceptionHandler.handleBadRequestException already owns (GlobalExceptionHandler.java:182-192). The copies differ: the handler adds the traceId property from MDC, this one does not, so a missing-header 400 is the only bad-request response without a trace id.
todos.fix: Must: one place builds the bad-request ProblemDetail, and the filter's 400 carries the same fields (including traceId) as every other 400. One way: extract a static ProblemDetails.badRequest(detail) factory used by both GlobalExceptionHandler and this filter, or delegate to HandlerExceptionResolver with a BadRequestException.

todos.issue: servletPath(request) (lines 89-100) does not always return the servlet path: when getServletPath() is empty it returns the request URI minus the context path, or the raw URI. The name's value word does not cover those values. It is also package-private static with no caller outside the class.
todos.fix: Must: the helper's name says it returns the path within the application, whichever source it read, and it is private. One way: rename to pathWithinApplication and make it private (or use Spring's UrlPathHelper.getPathWithinApplication and delete the helper).

todos.issue: The logger is looked up per call with a fully qualified org.slf4j.LoggerFactory.getLogger(...) at line 79, and java.net.URI is fully qualified at line 83, instead of @Slf4j and imports as RequestTracingFilter and GlobalExceptionHandler do. The com.fasterxml import (line 16) also sits after the org.springframework block.
todos.fix: Must: the class logs through a @Slf4j log field and imports URI, matching sibling filters. One way: add @Slf4j, import java.net.URI, and order imports as the repo's formatter does.
